content:
## Product overview

Purpose: Provide a single-source reference for Unified Inference (hosted Redwood API + Dedicated + Private variants) product direction, engineering requirements, design constraints, commercialization approach, and release notes for v1.4 (Nov 2026). The goal is to reduce ambiguity across teams during the launch window and subsequent Q1 2027 roadmap.

Key value propositions:
- Unified API and operational model across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Cost-aware routing and automated fallbacks to maintain availability under constrained capacity.
- Production-grade observability and rollout tools for model versioning and rollback.

Primary personas:
- ML engineers integrating inference into product features.
- Platform engineers operating Dedicated/private deployments.
- Product managers and GTM teams packaging offering for enterprise buyers.

=== Goals and success metrics ===
1) Reliability: 99.95% uptime for Hosted API endpoints (SLA tier 1).
2) Latency: P95 generation latency <= 180ms for short completion workloads (<=512 tokens) on our default model profile.
3) Cost: Reduce median per-token compute cost by 12% vs v1.3 through smarter batching and quantization defaults.
4) Adoption: 30 enterprise pilots for Dedicated/Private by end of Q1 2027.
5) Quality: No more than 1.5% regression on regression-suite prompt sets after rollout.

=== Product requirement summary (PRD) ===
Scope: This PRD covers v1.4 improvements across API capabilities, runtime behavior, deployment controls, and pricing. Excluded: Deep model architecture research and major compiler rewrites (targeted to v2.0).

High-level requirements (must-have):
- API: Support streaming completions with tool/function-calling metadata (headers & schema annotations).
- Model variants: Introduce 'cost-aware' model variants (quantized 4-bit option + 8-bit fallback).
- Routing: Policy engine to route by latency budget, cost target, and customer tier. Policies configurable via Redwood Console.
- Observability: Token-level cost attribution and per-route latency heatmaps in Console.
- Rollouts: Canary + automatic rollback based on error-rate and quality regressions tied to prompt sets.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- Security: Audit logging for model selection and routing decisions; KMS integration for Private deployments.
- Scalability: Dedicated pools must support linear autoscaling to 500k tokens/sec aggregate per-customer for standard GPU profiles.
- Backwards compatibility: Existing API surface and SDKs must continue to function; new features opt-in.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Streaming handshake succeeds and client receives chunked responses with metadata; test harness shows 0 dropped chunks in 1000 CI runs.
- Routing policy changes applied via Console within 30s and are visible in the audit log.
- Canary deployment triggers rollback when error rate > 2% or quality drift > 1.5% within 10k sampled requests.

=== Detailed requirements and user stories ===
1) Feature: Cost-aware Model Variants
- User story: As an ML engineer, I want a lower-cost quantized variant so I can reduce inference spend for high-volume endpoints while preserving output quality.
- Acceptance: Endpoint can be pinned to `model-x-quantized-4b` and runtime falls back to `model-x-8b` when latency SLO is threatened.

2) Feature: Routing Policies
- User story: As a platform owner, I want to route requests by latency budget and customer tier so high-priority traffic gets low-latency capacity.
- Acceptance: Policy engine exposes JSON policy object via Console & API; simulated traffic verifies routing behavior per policy matrix.

3) Feature: Token-level Cost Attribution
- User story: As a finance analyst, I want per-route cost breakdowns to reconcile customer billing and internal optimization.
- Acceptance: Console displays token counts, compute-cost estimate, and storage cost per route for the last 30 days.

=== Design specifications ===
Overview: v1.4 design iterates on runtime kernel selection, routing orchestration, and Console controls. Components: Serving Runtime, Policy Engine, Console, Metrics Pipeline.

Architecture (textual diagram):
- Client -> Redwood API Gateway -> Policy Engine -> Router -> Serving Runtime (GPU pool) -> KV/Prefix Cache -> Response Stream
- Observability agent emits: request traces, token metrics, model-selection events to Metrics Pipeline (Prometheus -> ClickHouse).

API design notes:
- New optional header: `X-Redwood-Policy: <policy-id>` to force-evaluate a specific routing policy for testing.
- Streaming frame format: JSONL frames with fields {"chunk": string, "meta": {"model_variant": string, "seq_idx": int}}.

Runtime behavior and fallbacks:
- Default execution path: try quantized-4b model variant; if P95 latency exceeds configured budget or token-drop detected, dynamically switch to 8-bit variant for that request.
- Graceful degradation: if all variants fail or capacity exhausted, return standard structured fallback response with error-code `capacity_exhausted` plus a model-simulated short answer if `enable_fallback_simulation=true`.

Data and storage considerations:
- KV cache TTL default: 2 hours per-customer; configurable to 0/never for privacy-sensitive customers.
- Logs: model-selection events retained 180 days in ClickHouse for auditing.

Operational runbook excerpt (rollout & rollback):
1) Create release branch and tag v1.4-rc in `eng-serving-runtime`.
2) Deploy canary to 3% traffic for Hosted; spin up Dedicated pilot clusters per-customer with `--v1.4` flag.
3) Monitor: P95 latency, error rate, quality regressions against `regression-prompt-set-v1`. Thresholds: error rate > 2% or regression > 1.5% -> pause rollout.
4) If paused, run triage checklist: inspect kernel selection logs, check GPU memory fragmentation, check policy-engine logs for misrouting.
5) Rollback: revert to v1.3 tag and clear new policies. Notify stakeholders via #prod-deployments channel and file postmortem if rollback triggered.

=== Roadmap & themes (Q4 2026 - Q2 2027) ===
Themes for next two quarters:
- Q4 2026 (v1.4): Unified routing policies, cost-aware variants, Console observability for token-level cost; GA for Hosted improvements, Beta for Dedicated/Private.
- Q1 2027: Dedicated pilots and Private enterprise packaging, expand quantized model catalog, enable per-route billing exports.
- Q2 2027: Autoscaling policy refinements, workload classifier to auto-select model variant by request type, tighter SLO SLAs for enterprise tiers.

Milestones and dates:
- 2026-11-15: Internal feature-complete freeze (this doc created).
- 2026-11-30: Publish PRD and release notes (current doc).
- 2026-12-10: Begin Hosted canary ramp.
- 2026-12-20: Hosted GA for v1.4 (standard customers).
- 2027-01-15: Dedicated pilot onboarding (first 10 customers).
- 2027-03-31: Dedicated & Private GA readiness target.

=== Pricing & packaging notes ===
Pricing principles:
- Keep simple self-serve pricing for Hosted to preserve PLG motion; provide premium enterprise pricing for Dedicated and Private.
- Charge separate components: compute (per-token), storage (per-GB-month for KV/cache retention), and premium features (observability retention, SLAs).

Suggested packaging (v1.4):
- Hosted (Self-serve):
  - Free tier: 500k tokens/month trial.
  - Pay-as-you-go: $0.0009 per generated token on default model (post-discount).
  - Cost-aware variant discount: 20% lower per-token rate when endpoint pinned to quantized-4b.
- Dedicated (Committed):
  - Monthly reserved capacity tiers (S, M, L): base fee + per-token overage. Example: S: $12,000/month + $0.0006/token overage.
  - SLAs available at enterprise tier (99.95% uptime, dedicated on-call).
- Private (On-prem/VPC):
  - Licensing + support: annual platform fee + per-seat & professional services for deployment.
  - KMS/HSM integration and extended audit retention as add-ons.

Billing & reconciliation notes:
- Token-level cost attribution will feed Billing exports (CSV/BigQuery) daily. Finance to validate mapping and reconcile with ClickHouse compute cost estimates for first 3 months post-launch.

=== Release notes (v1.4) ===
Release tag: v1.4 (published 2026-11-30)
Highlights:
- Introduced cost-aware model variants (quantized 4-bit) with dynamic runtime fallback.
- Policy Engine UI: create & apply routing policies by latency or cost target.
- Token-level cost attribution surfaced in Console (per-route).
- Streaming API updates: metadata frames and `X-Redwood-Policy` test header.

Fixed in this release:
- Resolved memory leak in runtime kernel selector that affected long-running streams (issue #SRT-423).
- Fixed inconsistent canary metric aggregation that caused delayed rollback signals (issue #OBS-334).

Known limitations and mitigations:
- Quantized variants may show minor quality regressions on long-context completion tasks (>2048 tokens). Mitigation: automatic fallback to 8-bit variant for long contexts and guidance in Console.
- Billing accuracy for new per-route cost attribution is initially estimated; Finance should expect +/- 3% variance during first 30 days while accounting calibration completes.

Rollout plan (summary):
- Hosted: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with continuous quality checks.
- Dedicated: Pilot customers onboarded individually with dedicated runbooks; expand to commit tiers after successful pilot.
- Private: Customer opt-in via on-prem package with support; KMS integration as a prioritized onboarding task.
